sections.h2: Where Branch County records deeds and mortgages
sections.html:
Branch County land records are kept in the Courthouse Annex, 23 East Pearl Street, Coldwater. Weekday counter hours are 7:30 to 4:30, lunch hour included, and the office phone is 517-279-4320.

A document that arrives after the 4:30 close still gets that day's date stamp, and the clerks record it first thing the following morning. E-recording is accepted, which suits lenders and title agents closing a Coldwater, Bronson or Quincy sale from a distance. Frequent researchers can pay monthly for remote access, and occasional ones pay per search.

An owner checking for back taxes before listing can use the treasurer's free delinquent tax search at bsaonline.com. Under Online Services choose Delinquent Tax Search, then enter a surname, a parcel number or a street address.

Each recording costs $30 flat. The county forwards $4 of every fee to the state survey and remonumentation fund, with carve-outs for fixture filings, liens filed by the state or federal government, state deeds, plats and tax reversion documents. The governing fee statute is MCL 600.2567.

  • $30 each for a deed, a mortgage, a lien notice or release, and a UCC fixture filing.
  • $3 for every instrument past the first on a combined assignment or discharge.
  • $1 per page for copies of recorded real estate documents, and $5 to certify a document.
  • Name searches at 50 cents per year searched, never less than $5, and $3 per name for a lien search.
  • $5 to have a document faxed or emailed.

Mailed submissions must include a stamped envelope addressed to you, since that is how the recorded original comes back.

Returned paper usually fails one of the formatting tests in MCL 565.201. Check these points first.

  • A typed or printed name beneath each signature, which should be dark ink and must spell the name the way the notary block does.
  • The notary's printed name sitting near the notary signature on the same sheet.
  • Grantee mailing addresses, plus who drafted the paper and where to reach them.
  • An unprinted strip of 2 1/2 inches on top of page one, and 1/2 inch along all remaining edges.
  • A heading line that states the single recordable event, for example warranty deed.
  • Dark print of at least 10 points on white stock weighing 20 pounds, no smaller than letter and no longer than legal.
  • Social Security numbers cut to their last four digits, and a written English translation for foreign-language text.

Once a document meets these tests, the register cannot refuse it over what it says.

That turns on the kind of deed. Warranty deeds, deeds with a warranty covenant, land contracts and land contract memoranda with a warranty clause all go through the Branch County Treasurer first. MCL 211.135 is the source, and the certificate has to show that the parcel carries no tax liens or tax titles and that five years of taxes before the deed date are settled.

The treasurer charges $5 a document for as many as five descriptions and 20 cents for each one beyond five. That money goes on its own check made out to the Treasurer's Office.

A quitclaim with no warranty covenant sits outside the rule, so family transfers and title fixes tend to move quickly. If you owe back taxes, expect a warranty deed to sit until the balance is paid.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Branch County sale
sections.html:
A sale draws two levies. The county takes 55 cents for every $500 of value or fraction (MCL 207.504), and the state takes $3.75 on the same unit (MCL 207.525). Added together, that is $4.30 per $500 and $8.60 per $1,000. The deed should state the full value on its face, or an affidavit of value goes with it.

Branch County transfer tax rates
TaxRate per $500 of value or fraction
County$0.55
State$3.75
Combined$4.30

The Register of Deeds collects the tax on any transfer of $100 or more and publishes a rate schedule on its resources page. Who pays is settled in the purchase agreement.

County and state exemptions overlap without matching exactly. Both let through nominal deals under $100, mortgages and other security papers, leases, court orders that name no price, boundary corrections, title-confirming quitclaims, and land contracts whose legal title has not yet passed.

  • A parent or grandparent deeding to a descendant, including step and adopted relations, is exempt only in the state act, MCL 207.526.
  • Foreclosure is treated differently too. The state exempts any mortgage foreclosure or deed in lieu, while MCL 207.505 reaches only government-made, guaranteed or insured loans.
  • The county list carries no gift-to-child entry, so ask in Coldwater whether the county's 55 cents still hits a family deed.

The Coldwater office records land for every parcel in the county, wherever it sits. The two cities are Bronson and Coldwater. Quincy, Sherwood and Union City are villages. The sixteen townships are Algansee, Batavia, Bethel, Bronson, Butler, California, Coldwater, Gilead, Girard, Kinderhook, Matteson, Noble, Ovid, Quincy, Sherwood and Union.

Unincorporated places on the county's list include Canada Shores, Crystal Beach, East Gilead, Girard, Hatmaker, Hodunk, Lockwood, Pearl Beach, Ray and Sans Souci Beach. A deed for a lot in any of them goes to the same counter in Coldwater.

sections.h2: Branch County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Coldwater is the seat and biggest city, and farming is still the base of the local economy. The 2025 population estimate is 45,993, with 21,287 housing units and 16,906 households. Owners occupy 77.7% of units, the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $162,500, and gross rent in the middle of the range is $959. Because the recording fee, the tax certificate and the transfer tax all come out at closing, ask your title agent for the totals before you sign.

Typical sequence for a sale: check for back taxes, get the treasurer's certificate if the deed carries a warranty, sign a deed that meets the format rules, and have the title agent record it, electronically if you are out of town. A cash buyer who takes the house as-is can shorten the repair and lender steps, but the recording requirements stay the same.

faqs.q: How much will I pay to put a deed on record in Branch County?
faqs.a: Budget $30 for the recording itself, no matter how many pages the deed has. Add $3 per extra instrument if one document assigns or discharges several, and at least $5 for the treasurer's certificate when the deed carries a warranty.

faqs.q: What are the street address and hours of the Branch County recorder?
faqs.a: Go to the Courthouse Annex at 23 East Pearl Street in Coldwater between 7:30 and 4:30 on a weekday. The number to call is 517-279-4320.

faqs.q: Does Branch County take electronic filings?
faqs.a: It does. Electronic submissions are accepted, and whatever lands after 4:30 in the afternoon is date stamped that day and entered in the books the next morning.

faqs.q: Is a tax certificate needed to record a quitclaim in Branch County?
faqs.a: Usually not. The tax certificate statute, MCL 211.135, carves out a quitclaim or any deed lacking a covenant of warranty. Warranty deeds and land contracts still need the county treasurer's sign-off.

faqs.q: What happens with transfer tax when I deed the house to my son or daughter?
faqs.a: The state tax does not apply, because MCL 207.526(j) and (k) exempt a transfer to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild. The county statute lists no such exemption, so ask the Register of Deeds about the county's 55 cents per $500 before you record.
